findings.namedBuyers: Primary: Ann-Marie Rasiawan, Conference Planner, University of Toronto CPD, named in the 2026 event prospectus; relevant operational entry point, with sponsorship responsibilities explicitly documented. Secondary: Nancy Carey, Associate Director, Conference Management, named in CPD’s official directory; relevant management-level referral/escalation contact, but no edition-specific housing responsibility established. Historical: Sandra Gauci, CMP, Event Planner, Department of Ophthalmology and Vision Sciences, named in the 2024 and 2025 prospectuses; not verified as 2026 planner. Clara C. Chan and Stephan Ong Tone sign the 2026 prospectus as program co-directors; academic influence does not establish hotel purchasing authority. None is publicly proven to control the accommodation contract.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming as of 2026-11-15: December 4–5, 2026, Toronto, Ontario, Canada; a two-day medical CME symposium, within the requested horizon. Both the official event homepage and edition-specific 65th Annual prospectus publish these activity dates. No official 2027 or 2028 edition dates or city announcement located; annual recurrence must not be converted into a dated future booking.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: the 157-room Harbourfront property is a plausible city-hotel alternative for a limited delegate, speaker, exhibitor or executive lodging allocation, not a resort-led incentive proposition. The official hotel block establishes some overnight accommodation provision, but not how many visitors need rooms. Do not assume the symposium is either too large or too small: organizer attendance and peak rooms are unpublished in reviewed sources. Do not propose exclusive housing or replacement of the MTCC programme. Side meetings are only a prospect, not a published requirement; any meeting allocation must respect the supplied ballroom capacities. Restaurant/lounge and catering availability remain unverified, so no catering promise is justified.
findings.venueCommitments: Officially published 2026 venue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, 100 Level, 255 Front St W, Toronto, Ontario. This is Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC, within the hotel’s supplied territory. The venue is a convention centre, not the accommodation hotel. Public designation is verified; an executed venue contract was not available.
findings.historicalRotation: Published timeline: 61st edition December 2–3, 2022; 62nd December 1–2, 2023; 63rd December 6–7, 2024; 64th December 5–6, 2025; all listed at MTCC in Toronto. The 2024 and 2025 official prospectuses specify North Building; 2026 returns there. Evidence supports repeated Toronto/MTCC use, not destination rotation. Archived web pages can inherit newer edition headers, so historical dates are taken from edition-specific PDFs and the Canadian Glaucoma Society calendar, not inherited headers.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Exactly one hotel is listed on the 2026 official accommodation page: The InterContinental Toronto Centre, 225 Front St W, Toronto. Quote: “A limited block of rooms is being held at The InterContinental Toronto Centre at the conference rate of CAD $359 per night (plus taxes).” Quote: “Rooms at the conference rate are available until the guestroom block fills or Tuesday, November 3, 2026, whichever occurs first.” Attendees book directly by telephone, referencing the Walter Wright Symposium group block, or through https://book.passkey.com/go/WalterWrightSymposium2026. Quote: “The sale of rooms booked under the group conference rate help to offset conference expenditures.” This establishes an edition-specific incumbent block, not a preferred-hotel list. No named external housing bureau, open accommodation RFP or additional official hotel was found. Passkey is a booking link, not proof of a separate housing buyer. The published cutoff has passed; this does not prove sellout or current availability.
findings.organizationStructure: University-led academic continuing medical education, not a corporate incentive programme or an independent membership association event. The Department of Ophthalmology & Vision Sciences presents the symposium; Temerty Faculty of Medicine Continuing Professional Development provides the published conference contact and conference-management team. MTCC is the event venue; InterContinental Toronto Centre is the published accommodation incumbent. No external PCO/DMC appointment was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The official 2026 accommodation block is already placed at InterContinental Toronto Centre, and the organizer says group-rate bookings offset conference expenditures. Inference: this creates a commercial reason to support the incumbent before adding alternatives. No evidence of hotel sellout, displaced delegates, block exhaustion, overflow appointment or unmet room demand was found. “Limited block” alone is not overflow evidence. No primary-source attendance, peak-room or room-night total was found. XPO Times publishes approximately 49 expected visitors without a visible methodology; treat this as an unverified third-party estimate, not a qualified attendance or lodging forecast.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Ann-Marie Rasiawan first with a short introduction and a request to identify the hotel-block decision maker. Ask whether any December 4–5, 2026 attendees still require rooms after cutoff, whether alternatives may be offered without undermining the incumbent block, and what peak rooms/stay pattern would be needed. Only then offer a small, inventory-dependent room allocation; do not assert a 15–109-room requirement. If no immediate need exists, request a post-event discussion of actual pickup and the next edition’s housing procurement timetable. Use Nancy Carey as a secondary management referral, not an assumed contract signatory. Verify hotel inventory and catering operation before proposing rates or functions.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2026 is still upcoming, but its venue and published hotel block are already designated and the November 3 accommodation cutoff is past as of November 15. Late supplemental lodging could only be pursued after direct confirmation of unmet need and organizer permission; no current open sourcing or sellout is verified. Do not retain the prior SALES_READY label as evidence.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Verified annual series and repeated Toronto/MTCC use justify relationship development for a later edition. Inference: seek an approved supplemental block or speaker/exhibitor allocation, rather than presume displacement of the incumbent or relocation of the conference. No 2027/2028 dates, venue commitment, accommodation RFP or buying window is publicly verified; future competitive capture remains conditional, not contracted demand.
